questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Angola?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Angola on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Angola article.

questions.proof: It shares borders with Namibia in the south, the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the north, and Zambia in the east.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Angola about 1,246,700 square kilometres; Republic of the Congo about 342,000 square kilometres; Uganda about 241,038 square kilometres; Burundi about 27,834 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Angola?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Angola article.

questions.proof: Angola's capital, and most populated city, is Luanda.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Luanda?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
